docs.t: Judge Randy Crane (S.D. Tex.) — Trial
docs.x: Judge Randy Crane, S.D. Tex.. Trial: Jury selection is set in the scheduling order (9:30 a.m. in the form order); the trial date is set at the final pretrial conference and is ordinarily later in the trial month. Provide a bench copy of all documentary exhibits (on disc in .pdf, .doc, or .wpd if voluminous). Mark each exhibit with party name, case number, and exhibit number, exchange before trial, and include exhibit lists in the joint pretrial order. Notify the offering party in writing within 5 business days after an exhibit is made available if you require authentication, or authenticity is admitted (L.R. 44.1). The court conducts preliminary voir dire; include proposed questions in the pretrial order and be ready to introduce co-counsel and likely witnesses. Get advance permission through the case manager to use any presentation equipment.

docs.t: Judge Randy Crane (S.D. Tex.) — Courtroom decorum
docs.x: Judge Randy Crane, S.D. Tex.. Courtroom decorum: Formal courtroom etiquette under Appendix C of the Local Rules and formal attire are required; counsel must tell witnesses and family members. Phones, laptops, and other wireless devices may be brought into the courthouse but not used in the courtroom without the judge’s approval, and no recording or photography without authorization. The procedures also say no weapons or cell phones are permitted in the courtroom unless they are evidence, so ask first.

docs.t: Judge Randy Crane (S.D. Tex.) — Settlement and recusal
docs.x: Judge Randy Crane, S.D. Tex.. Settlement and recusal: Notify the case manager immediately of any settlement, preferably by email. The court then vacates all settings, moots pending motions, and gives about three weeks to file dismissal papers. Settlements for a minor or incompetent plaintiff require a joint motion for an attorney ad litem if there is a potential conflict with the parent or guardian. Immediately tell the court of anything that may require recusal or might create an appearance of conflict, which may be done by letter to chambers copied to all counsel.

docs.t: Judge Rolando Olvera (S.D. Tex.) — Initial conference (trap)
docs.x: Judge Rolando Olvera, S.D. Tex.. Initial conference (trap): The judge holds the initial pretrial conference. At least 14 days before, file the joint case management plan (judge’s form, which also requires a list and summary of all pending issues that counsel have agreed on). At least 5 days before, file a joint proposed scheduling order using the court’s template. Plaintiff (or the removing party) must serve the Order Setting Conference, the case management plan form, and the proposed joint scheduling order form with the summons and complaint. Interested-parties lists are due within 15 days of the order. Counsel in charge must attend all hearings and conferences; a substitute needs a motion to appear, granted in advance for good cause, and must know the case and have authority to bind the client. Discuss ADR with clients and opposing counsel before the conference.

docs.t: Judge Rolando Olvera (S.D. Tex.) — Scheduling order deadlines (trap)
docs.x: Judge Rolando Olvera, S.D. Tex.. Scheduling order deadlines (trap): Under the judge’s template: new parties joined within 180 days of the complaint (or notice of removal); plaintiff’s experts 180 days and defendant’s experts 120 days before the discovery deadline; discovery closes 90 days before the joint pretrial order (JPO) deadline. Dispositive and nondispositive motions are due 30 days after the discovery deadline, with responses due 21 days after filing. Daubert motions and motions to exclude experts are due 60 days before the JPO deadline. The JPO, with witness and exhibit lists, is due 60 days before the final pretrial conference (3:00 p.m.); mediation and a status report are due 30 days after the JPO. Jury selection is at 10:30 a.m. Discovery motions to compel must certify a good-faith conference under Rule 37(a)(1), and all disclosures and discovery papers must be signed under R

docs.t: Judge Rolando Olvera (S.D. Tex.) — Exhibits and witness objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge Rolando Olvera, S.D. Tex.. Exhibits and witness objections (trap): Exchange all documentary exhibits on the day the JPO is filed (except rebuttal or unanticipated exhibits), marked with the date and case number. Objections to exhibits and witnesses, and written demands for authentication, are due 15 days after the JPO, with copies of the disputed exhibit and legal authority; responses are due 15 days later (30 days after the JPO). An unanswered objection is sustained, an exhibit or witness not timely objected to is admitted, and rulings are made on the papers. Motions in limine are due 15 days after the JPO, and responses 30 days after the JPO.

docs.t: Judge Rolando Olvera (S.D. Tex.) — Pretrial order contents
docs.x: Judge Rolando Olvera, S.D. Tex.. Pretrial order contents: The JPO follows the judge’s form, restating each instruction: statement of the case for the jury panel, jurisdiction, contentions, admitted and contested facts, agreed and contested law with authority, exhibit and witness lists, a statement that settlement efforts are exhausted, and trial length and logistics. Each party separately files, in duplicate, proposed voir dire and a proposed jury charge with authority (jury trials) or proposed findings and conclusions with authority (bench trials). If trial is estimated at more than 5 business days, each party must give specific, itemized time limits for each listed witness.

docs.t: Judge Rolando Olvera (S.D. Tex.) — Trial and courtroom conduct
docs.x: Judge Rolando Olvera, S.D. Tex.. Trial and courtroom conduct: At trial, a party’s first act in its case-in-chief is to offer its exhibits into evidence. Address the court as “your honor” or “Judge” and others by title and surname; stand when speaking to or addressed by the court. Approach the bench only with permission, hand items for the judge to the Case Manager only, and stay at counsel table during sessions and in attendance during jury deliberations. Don’t participate as trial counsel if you expect to be a witness, without permission.

docs.t: Judge Carol B. Whitehurst (W.D. La.) — Rule 26(f) report
docs.x: Judge Carol B. Whitehurst, W.D. La.. Rule 26(f) report: E-file the report and provide copies to opposing counsel. Affirm compliance with Rule 26(a)(1) initial disclosures by the scheduling-order deadline or explain why not; describe claims and responses without simply repeating the pleadings. The scheduling order already contains a discovery plan; propose a more case-specific one, or ask for a telephone conference with the magistrate judge, if needed. Also state whether “Phase II” discovery (Paragraph 8 of the scheduling order) is needed and identify any related federal or state case. Affirm that counsel learned the clients’ wishes on ADR before the conference and discussed ADR in good faith; if a judicial settlement conference would help, give four mutually convenient dates and times. Parties must first exhaust good-faith efforts to settle without the court.

Pretrial filings: Measured from the initial pretrial conference: motions in limine and deposition designations 14 days before; objections to designations and cross-designations 10 days before; responses to motions in limine and objections to cross-designations 7 days before; stipulations of uncontroverted facts and of admissibility, witness lists, and exhibit lists 3 days before. Jury instructions are due 14 days before trial; trial briefs and voir dire 5 days before trial. Chambers’ model jury instructions are posted on the judge’s page. The court typically resolves evidentiary objections at the pretrial conference and pre-admits as many exhibits as is reasonable. Give the court reporter a glossary of technical, medical, or unusual terms before hearings and at the pretrial conference.

docs.t: Judge Roseann Ambrosia Ketchmark (W.D. Mo.) — Jury selection, openings, and juror questions
docs.x: Judge Roseann Ambrosia Ketchmark, W.D. Mo.. Jury selection, openings, and juror questions: If the parties agree, the attorneys may conduct voir dire and give brief openings at the start of voir dire; otherwise the court conducts voir dire and allows brief follow-up by each side. If the parties agree, the jury is instructed on the law before openings. There is generally no time limit on openings. Jurors may take notes and may submit written questions after counsel finish with each witness; every juror turns in a card. The court reviews questions with counsel at the bench, where counsel may object or ask to revise the form. A criminal defendant who testifies may choose whether juror questions may be asked of the defendant.

docs.t: Judge Roseann Ambrosia Ketchmark (W.D. Mo.) — Trial conduct
docs.x: Judge Roseann Ambrosia Ketchmark, W.D. Mo.. Trial conduct: Trial runs 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday; substantive issues are taken up before 9, during breaks, or after 5 when possible. Counsel need not stay at the lectern but must not block anyone’s view; stand when addressing or addressed by the court. Address adult witnesses as “Mr.,” “Ms.,” or “Dr.,” never by first name. One attorney per party per witness, and the attorney who objects on direct conducts the cross (and vice versa). Approach without asking; state objections by legal ground only, arguing at the bench. Don’t ask to have a witness declared an expert. Offer or request stipulations at the bench, not in the jury’s hearing; written stipulations may be marked and read but generally don’t go to the jury room. Deposition guidelines: objections and instructions (trap): The judge’s Guidelines for Discovery Depositions are so ordered in every civil case and enforced on motions. At the start, deposing counsel must instruct the witness to ask deposing counsel, not the witness’s own counsel, for any clarification, and the witness must comply. Objections are preserved and must not be made during the deposition, except those waived if not made under Fed. R. Civ. P. 32(d)(3)(B) and those needed to assert a privilege, enforce a court-ordered limitation on evidence, or present a Rule 30(d) motion. Objections must be succinct, state only the basis, and not suggest an answer. Counsel may not instruct or ask a witness not to answer unless counsel has objected on privilege or a court-ordered limitation on evidence.

Any such conference, permitted or not, must be noted on the record by the participating counsel, with its purpose and outcome, and deposing counsel may inquire into it to find out whether there was witness coaching.

docs.t: Judge Leslie G. Foschio (W.D.N.Y.) — Deposition guidelines: documents and questioning
docs.x: Judge Leslie G. Foschio, W.D.N.Y.. Deposition guidelines: documents and questioning: Deposing counsel must give the witness’s counsel a copy of every document shown to the witness, either before the deposition or as each document is shown. The witness and counsel have no right to discuss documents privately before the witness answers questions about them. One question at a time; let the witness answer fully without interruption; no characterization of or comment on answers. If an answer seems unresponsive, say so and have the stenographer repeat the question; if a question is unclear, the examiner may rephrase or withdraw it. No argument between counsel over objections or the nature of questions; note the objection on the record and seek relief after the examination. Avoid unnecessary on-the-record recitation or lengthy quotation of documents.

docs.t: Judge Annie T. Christoff (W.D. Tenn.) — Criminal jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Annie T. Christoff, W.D. Tenn.. Criminal jury instructions: The judge posts a shell set of criminal jury instructions keyed to pattern-instruction section numbers (for example, 1.01–.09, 2.04–2.08, 7.01–7.21, and 8.01–8.10), with blanks for judicial notice, stipulations, opinion witnesses, and the offense elements. docs.t: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker (W.D. Tenn.) — Rule 26(f) report and proposed order
docs.x: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker, W.D. Tenn.. Rule 26(f) report and proposed order: Meet at least 21 days before the conference. File a written discovery-plan report and email a proposed scheduling order on Exhibit A to the chambers address at least 7 days before the conference, with case-specific dates rather than the form’s defaults. Cover the old Form 52 checklist: discovery subjects and phasing, ESI, privilege and FRE 502 agreements, numerical limits on interrogatories, requests for admission, and depositions (with hour limits), expert and supplementation dates, amendment, joinder, and dispositive-motion dates, settlement and ADR, and trial length. Raise jurisdiction, limitations, class certification, qualified immunity, and conflict-of-interest issues at the first possible occasion, no later than the initial Rule 16(b) conference.

docs.t: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker (W.D. Tenn.) — Standard-track schedule
docs.x: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker, W.D. Tenn.. Standard-track schedule: Exhibit A guidelines: joinder and amendment within 2 months of the conference; motions to dismiss within 3 months; ADR within 12 weeks; discovery closes 6 to 8 months after the conference; plaintiff’s experts 2 months and defendant’s 1 month before the close; Daubert and dispositive motions within 1 month after the close. The court may adopt a shorter schedule. The judge’s Standard Track form uses day counts: disclosures 14 days, joinder and amendment 60 days, and motions to dismiss 90 days after the conference; written discovery 30 days before the close; experts 60 and 30 days before; Daubert and dispositive motions 30 days after. Serve written discovery at least 45 days before the written-discovery deadline. Trials are set at 9:30 a.m., within 18 months of filing unless the calendar or complexity requires later. The

docs.t: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker (W.D. Tenn.) — ADR (trap)
docs.x: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker, W.D. Tenn.. ADR (trap): Besides the 12-week ADR deadline, the forms order the parties to complete ADR before the close of discovery. The mediator files a Mediation Certification within 7 days after the session, and the parties file a results notice within 7 days after that certification (L.R. 16.3(d)). If no mediator is agreed within 1 week of the conference, the court picks one.

docs.t: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker (W.D. Tenn.) — Motions and deadlines
docs.x: Judge Thomas Lee Robinson Parker, W.D. Tenn.. Motions and deadlines: The forms restate L.R. 7.2: proposed orders in word-processing format to the ECF mailbox and consultation before any motion except under Rules 12, 56, 59, and 60; failure to respond may be grounds to grant; no reply (other than on Rule 12(b) or 56 motions) without a motion for leave within 7 days of the response. Absent good cause, scheduling-order deadlines won’t be modified or extended.

docs.t: Judge Tu M. Pham (W.D. Tenn.) — Settlement conferences (trap)
docs.x: Judge Tu M. Pham, W.D. Tenn.. Settlement conferences (trap): Held at the Clifford Davis/Odell Horton Federal Building, 167 North Main Street, Suite 338, Memphis. Lead trial counsel must appear, and parties or corporate representatives with full authority to approve any settlement must be present in person, along with an insurer or indemnitor representative with authority to pay the full policy limits. Plaintiff must make a good-faith settlement proposal at least 14 days before the conference; defendant must make a good-faith counter-proposal at least 7 days before. At least 3 business days before, submit to ECF_Judge_Pham@tnwd.uscourts.gov an in camera statement covering the evidence and law, the relief sought (plaintiff itemizes damages; defendant lists mitigating factors), strengths and weaknesses, and settlement talks so far. Do not file it. Clear the entire day. The posted confidenti

docs.t: Judge Tu M. Pham (W.D. Tenn.) — Jury voir dire
docs.x: Judge Tu M. Pham, W.D. Tenn.. Jury voir dire: The court asks the whole panel 15 standard questions (case length, prior knowledge, acquaintance with parties, counsel, firms, and witnesses, prior lawsuits and claims, similar experiences, prior jury service, burden of proof, impartiality, and hardship). Each panel member then answers individual questions (name and age, residence, marital status, children, education, legal training, 10 years of employment for the juror and household adults, and hobbies). Attorneys then may ask additional questions.

docs.t: Judge Tu M. Pham (W.D. Tenn.) — Sample jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Tu M. Pham, W.D. Tenn.. Sample jury instructions: The page posts complete jury-instruction sets from past trials as samples: a standard set (Barnett), Title VII discrimination (Kumar), medical malpractice (Fabery and McDaniel), breach of contract and promissory fraud (Craftco), wrongful death and products liability (Vest), and personal injury (Lyons). The Fabery set cites T.P.I.–Civil pattern instructions.

docs.t: Judge Tu M. Pham (W.D. Tenn.) — Scheduling orders
docs.x: Judge Tu M. Pham, W.D. Tenn.. Scheduling orders: The page links the district’s Local Rule 16.2 Standard, Expedited, and Complex Track scheduling-order templates (identical on every judge’s page). They set motion-to-compel deadlines of 45 days after the default or response (30 days if it falls within 30 days of the discovery deadline), require a proposed order in word-processing format to the presiding judge’s ECF mailbox and consultation before most motions, and bar replies without leave except on Rule 12(b) and 56 motions.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Motions practice (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Motions practice (trap): Before filing any motion, meet and confer on its substance and state in the motion whether it is opposed (in a criminal case, also probation’s position where appropriate). Label joint, uncontested, and agreed motions as such in the title and body. The page limits in N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e) are strictly enforced. Oral argument on civil motions is granted only in exceptional cases. Extension motions must state opposing counsel’s position and be filed as far ahead as possible; the court expects scheduling-order deadlines to be met. No off-the-record inquiries about when a substantive motion will be decided. Once a summary judgment motion has been fully briefed for 180 days, or any other motion for 90 days, counsel may file a status report on the motion’s effect on the parties and the case.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Filing order and citation format (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Filing order and citation format (trap): File the motion and its exhibits before the supporting brief, so the brief can cite their docket numbers. Exhibits may be attached to the motion or filed separately (the motion first, with an appendix); a response, reply, or surreply with exhibits starts with an appendix of exhibits. Give each e-filed exhibit a number and a descriptive name (for example, “Ex. 1—Smith Dep.”), not just “Exhibit 1.” Cite the docket entry, attachment, and .pdf header page, as in “(ECF 42-8 at 5)”; for depositions add page and line, as in “(Johnson Dep. Tr. 10:4–13, ECF 38-2 at 3).” Hyperlinks to cited law are preferred but not required.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Summary judgment (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Summary judgment (trap): A party planning a summary judgment motion must first ask the other parties whether they also plan to file one. Cite specific evidence for every fact; unsupported facts may be disregarded. Statements of undisputed material facts and responses are filed separately from the briefs, with line, paragraph, or page cites. In complex cases an agreed timeline of events is helpful. Deposition cites need page and line, and the exhibit must include the cited pages plus at least three pages before and after; motions lacking the excerpts may be summarily denied. Cross-motions follow an automatic four-brief schedule (motion; cross-motion and response; reply and cross-response; cross-reply), using the CM/ECF events specified. Motions to strike are strongly disfavored; argue admissibility in the briefs, and if a motion to strike is truly warra

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Other motions
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Other motions: When a complaint is amended as of course after a Rule 12 motion, the court’s standard practice is to deny the pending Rule 12 motion as moot. Rule 702 motions are not motions in limine: file them by the scheduling-order deadline, with any summary judgment motion or no later than the dispositive motion deadline. TRO and preliminary injunction motions must address each Rule 65 requirement plus when the irreparable harm will occur, any discovery needed, whether an evidentiary or argument hearing is sought, and a proposed timeline. Criminal motions: both the local criminal and civil rules apply. Written motions are preferred over oral ones, and stipulated or agreed motions are appreciated.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Trial setting and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Trial setting and continuances (trap): Civil trial dates are not set until the dispositive motion deadline has passed and dispositive and Rule 702 motions are decided. A motion to set trial earlier must state whether it is a jury trial, the expected length, proposed dates (at least 180 days after an unexpired dispositive deadline), and opposing counsel’s position. Trial scheduling conferences are by video; be ready to report on settlement, offer trial dates starting 6 months out, and flag trial issues. Pretrial deadlines, usually starting ten weeks before trial, come in the Order for Civil Trial, Final Pretrial Conference, and Order Controlling the Case. Criminal trial dates are usually set at arraignment. A motion to continue trial must include a speedy trial waiver signed by the defendant (by hand or electronically).

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Final pretrial conference and jury selection
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Final pretrial conference and jury selection: The final pretrial conference covers settlement or plea status, witnesses, exhibits and objections, motions in limine, deposition designations, stipulations, voir dire, time limits for openings and closings, witness separation, and daily schedules. Raise non-routine legal or evidentiary issues there after conferring. Counsel receive a link to juror questionnaires by noon on the Friday before trial (hard copies can be reviewed in the Clerk’s Office after noon that day). Refer to jurors only by number. Civil: usually eight jurors, no alternates, and at least three peremptories per side (exact number set at the final pretrial conference). Criminal: twelve jurors and two alternates, ordinarily 6 government and 10 defense peremptories plus one each for alternates. The court posts its standard criminal voir dire

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Courtroom conduct and objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Courtroom conduct and objections (trap): Stand when speaking and address the court, not opposing counsel. Openings, closings, and examinations are from the lectern; ask permission to leave it or approach a witness. Request that the court designate a witness as an expert after laying qualifications. No exhibit in opening without court approval unless admissibility is stipulated. A plaintiff suggesting a damages number must state it in the opening segment of closing, must reserve rebuttal time on the record, and must spend most of the time in the opening segment. Stand to object and state only the grounds; no further argument without permission. Only the lawyer who handled direct may object during other counsel’s examination of that witness, and only the lawyer who will cross may object during direct.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Depositions at trial
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Depositions at trial: Agreed deposition summaries are strongly urged, especially for any deposition over forty-five minutes, but are allowed only by stipulation. Edit transcripts and videos with opposing counsel to cut unnecessary material. Read-in testimony uses a person in the witness box reading the answers; the marked original transcript (and any video) is offered as an exhibit but not sent to the jury. Resolve objections made at the deposition before the final pretrial conference. Deposed treating physicians are presumed unavailable under Rule 32(a)(4); a written objection showing good cause must be filed at least 30 days before trial.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Exhibits (trap): Mark exhibits with Clerk’s Office stickers before trial (plaintiff numbers, defendant letters; re-mark deposition exhibits), paginate every page, and staple multi-page exhibits unless in a tabbed binder. Prepare 4 tabbed exhibit binders (bench, courtroom deputy, witness stand, opposing counsel) plus an empty tabbed jury binder kept by the deputy and filled as exhibits are admitted; three-hole punch all exhibits in advance. Get leave of court before publishing admitted exhibits to the jury. Show demonstratives to opposing counsel before trial; only unopposed ones may be shown without leave. Arrange oversized exhibits with the deputy at least two weeks before trial, and substitute photographs for drugs, currency, firearms, and other dangerous items.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Jury instructions
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Jury instructions: The court prepares all standard opening, closing, and general instructions. Deadlines to confer and submit proposed instructions and verdict forms are set in the Order for Civil Trial or the criminal Discovery and Scheduling Order. Use the Seventh Circuit Pattern Jury Instructions first, then other circuits’ patterns and the Indiana patterns, and include points and authorities with each proposed instruction. Instructions are settled at a conference near the close of evidence, before closings.

docs.t: Judge Cristal C. Brisco (N.D. Ind.) — Trial logistics
docs.x: Judge Cristal C. Brisco, N.D. Ind.. Trial logistics: Trial days generally run 9:00 a.m. to about 5:00 p.m. Be in the courtroom 15 minutes early each day and 30 minutes early on day one, and give the deputy an updated witness list with phonetic spellings at the first-day attorney conference. Do not run out of witnesses. A witness both sides will call is usually examined fully in the plaintiff’s or government’s case-in-chief. Arrange daily or realtime transcripts with the court reporter at least two weeks before trial, and give the reporter a list of unusual terms and names. Coordinate equipment use and training with the deputy at the final pretrial conference.

File a separate appendix of evidence as the primary docket entry, with an index describing each exhibit (e.g., “Jane Doe’s Deposition . . . Exhibit 1”) and each exhibit as its own separately titled, text-searchable attachment; never attach exhibits to the motion, brief, or statement of material facts. A courtesy binder (double-sided) is encouraged for large records and may be ordered. Cite exhibits with particulari

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — “Speed bump” deadline (trap)
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. “Speed bump” deadline (trap): The court sets a “speed bump” 30 days before the close of discovery. It is the deadline for motions to extend discovery or continue other pretrial deadlines; after it passes, such motions are approved only for extraordinary reasons directed to the presiding judge, and good cause alone is not enough. File motions to compel and other schedule-affecting motions early enough to allow briefing and a ruling before the speed bump. Discovery motions filed during the speed-bump period or after discovery closes ordinarily go to Judge Leichty rather than the magistrate judge.

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Motions, contact, and chambers copies
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Motions, contact, and chambers copies: Briefing schedules and page limits follow Local Rule 7.1 (as the page cites it). Courtesy hard copies are ordinarily unnecessary but are encouraged for complex filings. Status, scheduling, settlement, and other non-merits inquiries may go to the case manager or law clerks; never discuss the merits with staff. Copy all parties on any email to chambers.

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Case management and trial setting
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Case management and trial setting: The magistrate judge holds the Rule 16(b) conference about 30 days after the last party appears; counsel must attend unless excused, and must come prepared to discuss summary judgment and narrowing of issues. The resulting scheduling order and Memorandum of Status Conference change only for good cause. Trial is set at a status conference about 30 days before discovery closes. Criminal trials take precedence; counsel wanting more certainty may consent to the magistrate judge (the judge does not see who declined consent). Private ADR is encouraged; a magistrate judge settlement conference is available in an appropriate case. Under the COVID-19 tab, status conferences are held by telephone.

docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Civil pretrial deadlines (trap): At least 28 days before the final pretrial conference, exchange (not file) witness lists and deposition excerpts, exhibit lists and exhibits (not demonstratives), and contentions. At least 21 days before, exchange objections to witnesses, depositions, and exhibits, and proposed joint jury instructions. At least 14 days before, file evidentiary objections or motions to exclude experts (unless due sooner), plaintiff’s trial brief, proposed instructions, verdict forms, and voir dire questions (also emailed to chambers), the motion in limine, and the proposed final pretrial order. At least 7 days before, file opposing trial briefs, objections to instructions, verdict forms, and voir dire, and responses to motions in limine. The final pretrial conference is treated as the first day of trial; the final pretrial order will be

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Motions in limine and trial briefs
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Motions in limine and trial briefs: Only one motion in limine per party (with as many issues as needed), with supporting memoranda, at least 14 days before the final pretrial conference; responses at least 7 days before must state any part not opposed. Oral motions in limine only for good cause; rulings are interlocutory. Trial briefs are required unless excused and must cover issues, elements, stipulations, anticipated evidentiary and legal issues with authority, and each witness’s expected testimony.

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Exhibits (trap)
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Exhibits (trap): The parties must jointly prepare one set of exhibit binders and one flash drive (each exhibit a separate PDF) for the court, numbered (not lettered), with dividers; a joint exhibit list is preferred. Demonstratives go to chambers with the other exhibits by the same Wednesday deadline; objections to them are due by noon the Thursday before trial. New or modified demonstratives are barred at trial absent good cause.

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Civil jury selection and instructions
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Civil jury selection and instructions: The court conducts most voir dire and, in appropriate cases on request, allows a set time for attorney voir dire. The court gives Seventh Circuit civil instructions 1.01, 1.04, 1.06, 1.11-13, 1.27, and 1.32-34 in every case; parties must supply all substantive instructions. The instruction conference is on the record near the close of evidence, with a redline against the model instructions, and all instructions except those on deliberations are read before closing arguments.

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Trial conduct
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Trial conduct: Trial days run 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Time limits on openings and closings are set after consulting counsel. Have enough witnesses to fill the day, and raise out-of-sequence professional witnesses with opposing counsel first. Ask permission to approach the witness or bench; the podium is optional (in criminal trials, wear a microphone if not at it), and stand when examining or addressing the court. Avoid first names, never address a juror by name, and follow the Seventh Circuit’s Standards for Professional Conduct. State routine objections briefly in open court; speaking objections will be cut off, only the examining attorney may object for that witness, and no colloquy between counsel. Tell opposing counsel in advance of any non-oral opening presentation. For depositions played or read, give the courtroom deputy the transcript and a lis

docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Criminal pretrial (trap)
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Criminal pretrial (trap): The magistrate judge handles initial appearance, arraignment, and detention, and usually enters the standard scheduling order, with trial generally 45 to 60 days from arraignment; a notice of complex case filed before arraignment gets a trial-setting hearing before Judge Leichty. docs.t: Judge Damon Ray Leichty (N.D. Ind.) — Criminal trial
docs.x: Judge Damon Ray Leichty, N.D. Ind.. Criminal trial: Proposed final instructions (with authorities) and verdict forms are due by noon ET the Wednesday the week before trial, in Word (not PDF) to leichty_chambers@innd.uscourts.gov and filed; proposed voir dire questions are due by noon ET that Thursday. The court circulates its own sets first, so do not duplicate them. docs.t: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund (N.D. Ind.) — Motions and chambers copies
docs.x: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund, N.D. Ind.. Motions and chambers copies: Briefing schedules and page limits follow Local Rule 7-1. There are no motion days or motion calls. Extra chambers copies are ordinarily unnecessary, though the court may ask for a courtesy hard copy of a particularly lengthy filing. Discovery disputes are ordinarily referred to the assigned magistrate judge. Proposed orders go to the chambers mailbox.

docs.x: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund, N.D. Ind.. Settlement and trial setting (trap): Private ADR is encouraged; the court will refer a case to a magistrate judge for a settlement conference only on a showing that private ADR is inappropriate or has been tried without success. docs.x: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund, N.D. Ind.. Civil final pretrial and motions in limine (trap): A final pretrial conference precedes every jury trial. Motions in limine are due at least 14 days before the final pretrial conference, and each side may file only one (with any number of points). Each point must show why the evidence might be offered, why it is inadmissible, and what harm an in-trial objection would cause. docs.t: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund (N.D. Ind.) — Trial briefs (trap)

Each side has three peremptories, exercised one at a time, alternating from plaintiff; there are no backstrikes.

Openings and closings usually have no fixed limits beyond the time counsel request. Exhibits certain to be admitted and electronic presentations may be used in opening, but tell opposing counsel first. docs.x: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund, N.D. Ind.. docs.t: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund (N.D. Ind.) — Criminal pretrial and pleas
docs.x: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund, N.D. Ind.. Criminal pretrial and pleas: The magistrate judge handles the initial appearance, arraignment, and detention and enters a scheduling order setting trial within the 70-day speedy trial clock; Judge Lund then enters a supplemental order controlling the trial. Non-dispositive motions go to the magistrate judge, including motions to continue trial (state the length requested). Motions in limine, motions to suppress, and motions to continue sentencing go to Judge Lund. A discovery request beyond the standard discovery order must explain why that order is inadequate. After a plea agreement or notice of intent to plead is filed, the deputy schedules a change of plea hearing; if the judge is unavailable, the magistrate judge may take the plea with the parties’ consent.

File a pretrial statement addressing stipulations, exhibits and admissibility, experts, and the other matters in the standard scheduling order. docs.t: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund (N.D. Ind.) — Criminal jury instructions and selection
docs.x: Judge Gretchen Suzanne Lund, N.D. Ind.. Criminal jury instructions and selection: The court files its proposed final instructions and proposed voir dire questions first. Proposed voir dire questions must be filed, and a witness list sent to chambers, at least three business days before trial. Twelve jurors and two alternates for trials of two weeks or less; defense has 10 and the government 6 peremptories, plus one per side for every two alternates. docs.t: Judge Holly Ann Brady (N.D. Ind.) — Motions and hearings

Face-to-face meet-and-confer (trap): Civil: before filing any motion, counsel must meet and confer in person or by videoconference; telephone, email, or letters do not count without leave. Exceptions: TROs, joint motions, ex parte applications, motions involving a non-attorney pro se plaintiff, and motions during or after trial. The motion must include a certification or declaration giving the date and type of meeting. A noncompliant motion will be denied, and a nonmoving lawyer who refuses to confer may be ordered to pay expenses, including fees. Criminal: the same face-to-face conference and certificate are required before filing motions in limine, trial briefs, and proposed verdict forms, jury instructions, or voir dire questions.

docs.t: Judge Andrew G. Schopler (S.D. Cal.) — Sealing and redactions (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. Sealing and redactions (trap): Meet and confer on the narrowest possible sealing order before moving. Mark proposed redactions on the provisionally sealed version and explain in a table the grounds for each redaction; motions reciting only a general privilege category, or lacking a particularized explanation for every item, are summarily denied. A party relying on a transcript or audio/visual exhibit in court must give it to the other side early enough to confer on redactions or portions to be played; unresolved disputes require marked proposed redactions.

docs.t: Judge Andrew G. Schopler (S.D. Cal.) — Courtroom equipment, interpreters, and translations
docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. Courtroom equipment, interpreters, and translations: To use any electronic or audio/visual equipment in court, lodge a proposed order at least seven days before the appearance itemizing the equipment and dates; show the signed order to security. The party presenting foreign-language testimony must arrange the interpreter. Foreign-language exhibits need a translation plus a stipulation to it or a declaration that a court-approved translator did it.

docs.t: Judge Andrew G. Schopler (S.D. Cal.) — Civil summary judgment and settlement (trap)
docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. Civil summary judgment and settlement (trap): Meet and confer on a joint statement of undisputed facts, filed by the reply deadline. No separate statements of disputed or undisputed facts, and no argument in the joint statement, without leave. Notify the court and the magistrate judge immediately on settlement. The court typically won’t retain jurisdiction, but may grant a joint motion to dismiss retaining it if accompanied by a fully executed consent to magistrate judge jurisdiction over settlement disputes and the specified retention language in the motion and proposed order.

docs.t: Judge Andrew G. Schopler (S.D. Cal.) — Civil pretrial
docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. Civil pretrial: Unresolved disputes over redacting or excerpting transcripts or exhibits for trial, or over exhibits in opening statement, must be brought by motion in limine after conferring. Beyond CivLR 16.1(f)(6), the final pretrial order must include proposed verdict forms and voir dire questions and identify any portions not unanimously proposed. Email Word versions of verdict forms, voir dire questions, and jury instructions to efile_schopler@casd.uscourts.gov.

docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. All parties submit instructions, verdict forms, and voir dire questions, with the government identifying the joint ones (the defense need not file if it seeks nothing more), and email Word versions to chambers. Oral continuance motions are generally denied; file or email the request to the deputy by close of business two court days before the hearing (emergencies as soon as possible, explaining the exigency). docs.t: Judge Andrew G. Schopler (S.D. Cal.) — Jury selection and trial
docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. Jury selection and trial: Trials typically run 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Tuesday through Friday. The court sets a time limit per side, starting with openings; the deputy reports remaining time on request. Prospective jurors complete a worksheet of court- and party-set questions on day one, shared before selection; only the judge examines jurors unless ordered otherwise. For-cause challenges are made at sidebar (sustained jurors stay seated until peremptories finish); peremptories are simultaneous, written, and double-blind. Use the well only in openings and closings, question from the podium, keep witness-stand visits brief, and state only the legal basis of objections. Sidebars are strongly discouraged; raise issues before the jury arrives, at breaks, or after the day ends.

docs.t: Judge Andrew G. Schopler (S.D. Cal.) — Sentencing
docs.x: Judge Andrew G. Schopler, S.D. Cal.. Sentencing: Each party may submit no more than five sentencing letters; send additional ones to Probation for summary in the presentence report, or summarize them in the sentencing memorandum.

docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Remote appearance needs good cause (travel cost or convenience is not enough), a conference with opposing counsel, and a joint or ex parte motion filed at least 7 calendar days before the hearing; appearing remotely without approval can draw sanctions. No screenshots, recording, or rebroadcasting of remote proceedings. Argument is set for dispositive motions or when all counsel request it; the court tries to say at least a week ahead whether argument will be held. Ex parte and joint motions are not noticed motions.

docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Motion papers (trap): No courtesy copies unless ordered. Evidentiary objections go in the opposition or reply, count against page limits, and may not be filed separately. Separate statements of fact are not allowed without leave (Civ. L.R. 7.1(f)(1)). Errata and notices of errata are not permitted. Reconsideration motions: noticed, within Civ. L.R. 7.1(i)(1) time, no more than 10 pages with no attachments, addressing the federal standard without rearguing; the court sets opposition and hearing only if warranted, and all dates stay in place. docs.t: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia (S.D. Cal.) — Joint motions and continuances (trap)
docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Joint motions and continuances (trap): No stipulations; agreements needing approval are filed as joint motions (no hearing date needed). Email a Word proposed order to efile_battaglia@casd.uscourts.gov with every joint or ex parte motion; never file it on CM/ECF. Meet and confer before seeking to change any date. File the motion at least 7 days before the date to be changed, with a detailed declaration covering the original and proposed dates, good cause, prior requests and their outcome, the effect on other dates, and the meet-and-confer. Later requests must show excusable neglect.

docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Serve by fax, email with return receipt, or overnight mail. Opposition is ordinarily due by 5 p.m. the next business day (call chambers for more time); unopposed motions may be granted on that ground. Decided without a hearing unless the court sets one. When sealing another party’s confidential material, meet and confer with the designating party first; that party must supply the supporting declaration. Seek sealing before filing the related motion; if denied, the documents may be publicly filed. docs.t: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia (S.D. Cal.) — Criminal motions, bail, and pleas
docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Criminal motions, bail, and pleas: Motions (other than in limine and sentencing) at least 14 calendar days before the hearing; oppositions at least 7. Orders shortening time are disfavored and need a non-conclusory counsel affidavit; motions needing factual findings need declarations. Bail matters go to magistrate judges unless the case is set for trial, a plea was accepted, Judge Battaglia set the bond, or international travel is sought; then email a proposed order. Bail modification motions must state the positions of the U.S. Attorney, sureties, and Pretrial Services. Supervised release modification or termination motions must state the government’s and probation officer’s positions. Pleas generally go to magistrate judges; the judge may take one on calendar only if cleared with the deputy in advance.

docs.t: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia (S.D. Cal.) — Sentencing (trap)
docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Sentencing (trap): PSR objections and non-5K1.1 departure motions 14 days before; 5K1.1 motions, summary charts, addenda, and letters and documents 7 days before. Late filings mean a continuance unless counsel waive consideration of them. Each side gets up to 10 minutes to supplement on the record. Defense counsel must read, explain, and give the client the supervised release conditions before sentencing in felony cases. A PSR is required in all felony cases unless waived on a joint motion with the listed sentencing information (and, where applicable, an updated RAP sheet with detailed immigration history). To get probation’s supporting documents, confer with the officer and apply for an order.

docs.t: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia (S.D. Cal.) — Criminal trial
docs.x: Judge Anthony J. Battaglia, S.D. Cal.. Criminal trial: Trials run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Tuesday to Friday. Motions in limine are heard 14 days before trial, due 14 days before that hearing with oppositions 7 days before; no replies. Trial briefs are due with motions in limine; voir dire, joint and disputed jury instructions (emailed in Word), and witness and exhibit lists 7 days before trial. Examine from the podium or counsel table; permission to approach a witness is rarely granted (use the document camera). Lapel microphones must be used. No sidebars. Evidence is presented electronically (no binders). Counsel prepare two thumb drives (all marked and admitted exhibits for the record, and admitted exhibits only for the jury) with an agreed table of contents; discs are not accepted.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Hearing dates (trap)
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Hearing dates (trap): Under Civil Local Rule 7.1(b), get every civil motion hearing date by calling chambers. File and serve the motion papers within 3 court days of getting the date, or the reserved date is forfeited.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Oral argument (trap)
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Oral argument (trap): Civil motions are usually decided without argument. Unless told otherwise, put “PER CHAMBERS, NO ORAL ARGUMENT UNLESS REQUESTED BY THE COURT.” on the caption page of the notice of motion, directly under the hearing date. Any party may ask for argument in a separate filing explaining why it would help. A non-moving party’s request on a summary judgment motion will be granted. If argument is set, the court issues an order with the date and time. Junior lawyers: on request, the judge holds argument where attorneys admitted less than 5 years will argue for at least two opposing sides, or where one side’s attorney is admitted less than 5 years and the other side also requests argument. The lead attorney may also take part.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Briefing and evidentiary objections (trap)
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Briefing and evidentiary objections (trap): No separate statements of fact without leave of court. Objections to the moving party’s evidence go inside the opposition brief, and objections to the opposition’s evidence go inside the reply. Separately filed objections are stricken and not considered. Responses to objections in a reply may be made in a sur-reply of no more than 5 pages, limited to the objections; any other argument is disregarded. Otherwise, no sur-replies without leave.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Courtesy copies and proposed orders
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Courtesy copies and proposed orders: Filings over 20 pages, counting attachments and exhibits, must be mailed or hand-delivered to chambers within 24 hours after filing; urgent filings must be hand-delivered the same day. Tab exhibits when there are more than 3. Ask the case’s law clerk about binding or printing preferences. Proposed orders are required with all joint motions, stipulations, and applications or requests, but not with noticed motions. Do not e-file them: email them in Word or WordPerfect to efile_Moskowitz@casd.uscourts.gov, without the filer’s name or firm information.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Ex parte applications
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Ex parte applications: An application for relief not suited to a fully noticed motion may be filed without a hearing date and must be served on all parties. The court may rule without a response or may set a briefing schedule.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Sealing
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Sealing: A sealing request must give specific reasons; a “confidential” designation under a protective order is not enough by itself. If sealing is based on another party’s designation, meet and confer with that party beforehand, if feasible, about which documents it contends should be sealed.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Pretrial conference and motions in limine (trap)
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. The witness, exhibit, and deposition listings must include evidence anticipated for cross-examination, including impeachment evidence. Memoranda of contentions of fact and law are needed only for bench trials. The motion in limine hearing and the trial date are set at the pretrial conference. Typically each side may file 5 motions in limine of up to 5 pages each.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Criminal sentencing letters (trap)
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Criminal sentencing letters (trap): In criminal cases, no party may submit more than 5 letters about sentencing without leave for good cause. Extra letters may go to the probation officer preparing the presentence report, or be briefly summarized in a sentencing memorandum. Letters must be filed at least 5 days before sentencing and typed in at least 14-point font. Noncompliant letters are stricken, not read, and not part of the record.

docs.t: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz (S.D. Cal.) — Contacting chambers
docs.x: Judge Barry Ted Moskowitz, S.D. Cal.. Contacting chambers: Calls to chambers are allowed for scheduling and calendaring; staff cannot give legal advice or discuss the merits. Have the case number ready. Law clerks: (619) 557-5583.

Motions are generally decided on the papers. Argument will be held if attorneys admitted less than 5 years will argue for at least two opposing sides, or for one side and the other side also asks for argument; counsel must meet and confer and request it in writing at least 7 days before the hearing. Failure to oppose may be treated as consent. No sur-replies without leave. Exhibits must be excerpted to relevant material, non-duplicative, and clearly labeled, dated, and indexed.

The opposition must respond to that statement. Evidentiary and procedural objections must be filed with the opposition (or, for the movant, with the reply); if filed as a separate document, they are limited to 5 pages.

docs.x: Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks, S.D. Cal.. The court sets an opposition and hearing only if warranted after initial review, and all dates stay in place meanwhile. Daubert motions must be brought by the dispositive motion cut-off; they will not be heard as motions in limine.

docs.x: Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks, S.D. Cal.. Continuances, joint motions, and proposed orders: Meet and confer before seeking any continuance. If agreed, file a joint motion with a detailed declaration of reasons; if not, file an ex parte motion addressing diligence and prejudice and stating the original date, prior requests and their outcomes, and opposing counsel’s position. Proposed orders must accompany all joint and ex parte motions (not motions needing legal analysis, such as MSJs or Rule 12(b) motions), emailed in Word to efile_cheeks@casd.uscourts.gov, with no watermarks or firm insignia; continuance orders must show the current and proposed new dates. All stipulations must be filed as joint motions and have no effect until signed by the court.

docs.x: Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks, S.D. Cal.. Decided without a hearing unless the court sets one. In criminal cases, also submit the documents to be sealed, state the next hearing date, and email a digital courtesy copy of any sealed filing to the e-file address.

docs.x: Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks, S.D. Cal.. Communications, discovery, and appearances: No letters or emails to chambers unless requested. Telephonic appearances only in emergencies with court approval: leave a chambers voicemail at once, and have a colleague appear until permission is granted. In pro se prisoner cases, defense counsel must help arrange the prisoner’s appearance, including writs.

docs.x: Judge Jinsook Ohta, S.D. Cal.. Sealing: Sealing is strongly discouraged; agreement of the parties or a protective-order designation is not enough. docs.t: Judge Jeffrey T. Miller (S.D. Cal.) — Oral argument and briefing
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey T. Miller, S.D. Cal.. A movant who wants to submit on the papers should put “No Oral Argument Requested” in the caption. State all legal and factual bases in the opening brief; new matter in a reply, unless directly responsive to the opposition, may not be considered. A party that will not oppose must file a statement of non-opposition no later than 14 days before the hearing. Failure to file an opposition memorandum will be construed as consent to granting the motion. Motions for reconsideration are disfavored absent new evidence, a change in controlling law, or clear error.

docs.t: Judge Jeffrey T. Miller (S.D. Cal.) — Ex parte applications
docs.x: Judge Jeffrey T. Miller, S.D. Cal.. Ex parte applications: Ex parte applications need no hearing date. Administrative requests (enlarging or shortening time, exceeding page limits) are usually ruled on within 48 hours without a response; they must be served, and an opposing party must contact chambers immediately to ask to respond. True ex parte relief without notice is rarely appropriate unless authorized by statute and is subject to Fed. R. Civ. P. 65 and Civ. L.R. 83.3(h); the proponent must immediately contact chambers and request a hearing. For TROs or Rule 64 or 69 remedies, give notice to all interested parties, immediately inform chambers of the filing, and provide opposing counsel’s identity and contact information; staff will request a response and may request a reply or set argument.

The motion must specifically describe each document or portion and include a declaration showing compelling reasons (dispositive motions) or good cause; redactions must be highlighted or bracketed in the sealed lodgment and narrowly tailored. When sealing another party’s confidential material, first meet and confer with the designating party, which bears the burden and may file a supplemental brief or evidence.

docs.x: Judge Mary M. Rowland, N.D. Ill.. Settlement conferences before Judge Rowland (trap): Plaintiff’s letter (itemized damages and a risk-adjusted demand) goes to defense counsel 14 days before; defendant’s response 7 days before. Plaintiff emails all letters to Settlement_Rowland@ilnd.uscourts.gov 6 days before; do not docket them. Letters over 10 pages need a courtesy copy to the deputy at least 5 days before. Parties with full settlement authority (and insurer representatives) must attend in person; telephone availability is not allowed absent unusual circumstances. Verify any inability-to-pay claim beforehand, and bring a Medicare conditional payment letter where relevant. Sanctions may follow.
